sections.label: State land enforcement framework
sections.summary: PUB incurred additional costs from temporary flooding measures as encroachments impeded drainage works, and the Bill creates an enforcement framework to help SLA protect state land.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: However, in the intervening period, PUB incurred additional costs coming up with temporary flooding measures, as the encroachments impeded its drainage improvement works.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This Bill, if passed, will put in place an up-to-date and comprehensive enforcement framework, to better support SLA in protecting state land from misuse and damage.

sections.label: Penalty for unauthorised activities
sections.summary: Clause 5 sets a fine of up to $50,000 or up to six months' imprisonment, or both, for unauthorised activities on or damaging state land.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 5 prescribes a penalty comprising a fine of up to $50,000 or imprisonment for a term of up to six months, or both, for the offence of carrying out unauthorised activities on or damaging state land.

sections.label: Court-ordered monetary compensation
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Court order a convicted offender to pay the Government compensation, on top of any fine, for loss or damage from the offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill also provides that the Court may order a convicted offender to pay monetary compensation to the Government, on top of any fine imposed, for any loss or damage suffered by the Government due to the offence, such as de-contaminating polluted soil; the value of any forest products or other substances removed from state land; and the costs and expenses incurred by SLA in abating the encroachment.

sections.label: Interim injunction against suspected offender
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Commissioner of Lands to apply to a Court for an interim injunction against a person suspected of an offence before conviction, where imminent harm is unlikely to be addressed by an encroachment notice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Where there is imminent harm or danger that is unlikely to be effectively addressed by the issuance of an encroachment notice, the Bill empowers the Commissioner of Lands to apply to a Court for an interim injunction against a person suspected of an offence under the Bill, before the person is convicted.

sections.label: Streamlined process for encroachments
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a streamlined process for SLA to deal with encroachments more expediently, especially those posing public safety concerns or delaying redevelopment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill will introduce a streamlined process to enable SLA to deal with encroachments more expediently, especially those that may pose a public safety concern or delay redevelopment works on state land.

sections.label: Three-month claim period
sections.summary: Claimants now have three months after notice publication to make a claim to the land, instead of six months under SLEA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Claimants will also now have three months after the notice is published to make a claim to the land in question, instead of the six months under SLEA.

sections.label: Compounding minor offences
sections.summary: Authorised officers may compound minor offences by collecting a sum not exceeding the lower of $5,000 or half the maximum fine.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Authorised officers can also compound minor offences by collecting a sum not exceeding the lower of $5,000 or half the maximum fine prescribed for the offence.

sections.label: State land definition and agency powers
sections.summary: The Bill defines state land to avoid overlapping jurisdiction, ensuring PUB, NParks and LTA have sufficient enforcement powers as SLA does.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, the Bill defines "state land" in a way that avoids the overlapping of jurisdiction between the public sector agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These amendments will ensure that PUB, NParks and LTA will have sufficient powers to take enforcement action on state land under their respective legislation, as SLA does under this Bill.

sections.label: Accused must prove lack of knowledge
sections.summary: Under section 7, someone accused of unauthorised use of state land must prove they did not know and could not reasonably have known it was state land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 7, someone accused of unauthorised use of state land must prove that they did not know and could not have reasonably expected to know that the land was state land.

sections.label: Encroachment notice timeline requirement
sections.summary: Section 12(3)(a)(ii) requires an encroachment notice to state a timeline to comply and raise objections, but sets no minimum time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 12(3)(a)(ii) states that the encroachment notice must state a timeline to comply with the notice and to raise objections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, there is no requirement or guidance on the minimum time that must be provided.

sections.label: Clarifying abandoned land determination
sections.summary: The question asks how the authority will determine land is abandoned and for estimates of land that might be abandoned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify how the authority will determine that land is "abandoned"?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share some estimates of the amount of land that might be abandoned?

sections.label: Inspection timing for abandoned land
sections.summary: The question asks when and how long inspection takes before determining land has been abandoned for three years or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: When and how long does it take for the Government to conduct such necessary inspection before determining whether land has been abandoned for three years or more?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The house remained in a dilapidated state for more than a decade before the Public Trustee's Office took ownership in 2015.

sections.label: SLA and Public Trustee coordination
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SLA and the Public Trustee's Office will coordinate on similar situations, citing abandoned Chee Guan Chiang House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will there be a system of coordination between SLA and the Public Trustee's Office to better handle similar situations in the future?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Another example is the Chee Guan Chiang House, which has largely been abandoned.

sections.label: Managing abandoned properties
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will take proactive measures to quicken managing and inspecting abandoned properties under new laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the new laws in place, will the Government take proactive measures to quicken the process of managing and inspecting abandoned properties?

sections.label: Penalties against land encroachment
sections.summary: The passage supports higher penalties against land encroachment and misuse as deterrence, so reusing empty plots will not cost excessive resources and time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: When the time comes to put an empty plot into use, be it for building an HDB estate, a hospital, a public amenity and so forth, it will not cost excessive resources and time to reinstate it to a useable state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, support the higher penalties against land encroachment and misuse, which would serve as deterrence.

sections.label: Managing state lands effectively
sections.summary: The passage states that poorly managed lands inconvenience residents and calls for strong enforcement and streamlined measures to manage state lands effectively and efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: When these lands are not properly managed and issues simply take too long or even years to get settled by the Government, residents are inconvenienced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ensure that we have strong enforcement as well as streamlined measures to manage state lands in the most effective and efficient way.

sections.label: Higher fines for state land misuse
sections.summary: The passage states the maximum fine for unauthorised activities on state land will rise about 10 times to $50,000, and SLA encounters about 180 encroachment cases yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The maximum fine for all unauthorised activities on state land will be raised by about 10 times to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These retired seniors' activities hark back to a simpler time for them and are, generally, not harmful to themselves or others and it can prove very challenging for them to pay the higher penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that SLA encounters about 180 cases of encroachment every year.

sections.label: Singapore coral reefs lost
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's waters are among the world's busiest and home to over a third of world coral species, with about 60% of reefs lost to land reclamation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore's waters are some of the busiest in the world, but they are home to over a third of the world's coral species.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, about 60% of these reefs have already been lost to land reclamation.

sections.label: Environmental protection and development balance
sections.summary: A robust environmental framework would foreground protecting land, seabed and marine space while allowing sustainable tourism or commerce development, balancing stakeholders' needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Additionally, a more robust environmental protection framework would foreground the importance of protecting our precious land space, seabed and marine space while ensuring that any plans to develop tourism or commerce in these areas can be enacted in a sustainable way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While many of this Bill's amendments come across as administrative in nature, people do form emotional connections with their environments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With our limited resources, as we continue to develop regulations governing the space around us, we must balance different stakeholders' needs and wants while actively forecasting for the future.

sections.label: Maximum penalties, no minimum punishment
sections.summary: The Bill sets a maximum penalty because some trespass can cause severe damage, with no minimum punishment for any offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, sets out a maximum penalty since some forms of trespass can cause severe damage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Furthermore, for those prosecuted, the penalties imposed by the Court upon conviction will, ultimately, depend on the surrounding facts and circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: There is no minimum punishment for any of the offences in the Bill.

sections.label: Wholly accidental incursions not offences
sections.summary: Wholly accidental incursions would not be an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Wholly accidental incursions would not be an offence.

sections.label: Removal of fixed 28-day notice period
sections.summary: Removing the fixed 28-day notice period is intended to give SLA greater flexibility to deal with encroachments more expeditiously based on circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The removal of the fixed 28-day notice period is intended to provide SLA with greater flexibility to deal with encroachments more expeditiously, if appropriate or necessary, based on the circumstances of the case.

sections.label: Consistent and fair application of laws
sections.summary: Mr Yip pointed out that laws should be applied consistently and fairly to encroachments that could cause public obstruction or damage to state land.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Mr Yip rightly pointed out that our laws should be applied consistently and fairly when it comes to encroachments which could cause public obstruction or damage to state land.

sections.label: Refusal to comply without identification
sections.summary: Under clause 26, subsection (3), it is not an offence to refuse to comply with officers' orders if they do not declare their office or produce identification when asked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As stated in clause 26, subsection (3), if officers do not declare their office or produce their identification card when asked, it is not an offence for any person to refuse to comply with their orders.

sections.label: Forfeiture cases in past decade
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the forfeiture process, and about five cases occurred in the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the process of forfeiture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have encountered about five cases in the past 10 years.

sections.label: Reduced claim period and forfeiture
sections.summary: The reduced claim period will help expedite the forfeiture process so agencies can commence works on abandoned land for safety and health issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The reduced claim period will help to expedite the forfeiture process, so that agencies can commence any necessary works to address safety and health issues on the abandoned land.

sections.label: Determining abandoned land process
sections.summary: SLA will check with agencies to trace owners' whereabouts and will only commence forfeiture if land appears abandoned for three years or more and owners cannot be traced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As for Mr Louis Ng and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin’s queries on the process for determining if land is abandoned, SLA will carry out checks with agencies, such as the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority and the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, to trace the whereabouts of the owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: SLA will only commence the forfeiture process if it appears that the land has been abandoned for three years or more and the owners cannot be traced from SLA’s checks.

sections.label: Compensation after land forfeiture
sections.summary: After land is forfeited, a person who establishes a claim to SLA's satisfaction within six years from forfeiture can still receive compensation for the land's value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Even after the land is forfeited, any person who can establish a claim to the satisfaction of SLA, within six years from the date of forfeiture, can still be entitled to receive compensation for the value of the land.

sections.label: Enhanced enforcement framework and Southern Islands
sections.summary: The enhanced enforcement framework under the Bill will better support SLA in protecting state land in the Southern Islands from unauthorised use and damage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Generally, the enhanced enforcement framework under the Bill will also better support SLA in protecting state land in the Southern Islands from unauthorised use and damage.
